title: Fractional headroom hedging for spot evictions and GPU matching
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Background: We want to increase spot utilization to reduce unit inference cost while avoiding customer-visible regressions when spot VMs are reclaimed. Current fallback behavior indiscriminately falls back to on-demand with a full reservation shift which leads to sudden spend spikes and instability in GPU mix.

Goal: Implement a fractional headroom hedging (FHH) policy that maintains a small, dynamically computed on-demand headroom per region and customer segment to absorb spot evictions. Combine this with a cost-per-inference GPU scoring function so routing can prefer lower-cost GPU types while meeting latency SLO. The policy should respect per-customer budget caps and provide clear observability for spend variance.

Approach:
- Forecast-based headroom: use short-term spend + spot eviction probability forecasts to compute a fractional headroom ratio H(region,tier,customer) in [0, 1]. H is the percent of recent QPS to gate for guaranteed on-demand capacity rather than pure spot.
- Cost-aware GPU scoring: compute score = alpha * normalized_unit_cost + beta * SLO_penalty_estimate + gamma * cold_start_risk. Rank candidate GPUs (e.g., a100-q4, a100-q8, h100, t4) per request and try to schedule on the highest-ranked compatible device within the region.
- Budget caps integration: headroom calculation considers per-customer monthly/weekly spend caps so that hedging does not exceed cap burn-rate. If forecasted headroom would breach cap, degrade to stricter prioritization (latency over cost) or queue requests according to priority tiers.
- Smooth transitions: instead of instant failover to on-demand, throttle a fraction of requests into on-demand channels gradually over a configurable ramp window to avoid spikes.
- Simulation and offline tuning: implement a simulator that replays recent traffic traces, spot eviction traces, and price curves to tune alpha/beta/gamma and headroom floor/ceil.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Reserving headroom reduces theoretical cost savings but lowers spend volatility and tail latency regressions. We will provide knobs to tune aggressiveness per customer tier (e.g., enterprise vs. self-serve).
- Interaction with Dedicated pools: Dedicated customers already have reserved capacity; FHH only applies to hosted and burst-capacity scenarios.
- Cloud provider constraints: some providers expose instance preemption probabilities; others do not. The forecasting model should gracefully degrade to historical eviction rates per region/sku.

Metrics to track:
- Spend volatility (weekly) and delta vs baseline
- Spot eviction rate observed and requests shifted to on-demand
- Unit inference cost (cost per 1k tokens) by region and GPU type
- Latency P95/P99 for hedged vs non-hedged requests
- Fraction of requests hitting headroom quota vs overall

Rollout plan:
1) Simulation: build simulator and run against last 90 days of traffic. (2 weeks)
2) Internal canary: enable FHH for a small set of non-critical customers and internal traffic (10% of traffic) with observability dashboards and kill switch. (1 sprint)
3) Gradual customer opt-in: enable by default for self-serve customers at conservative defaults; offer controls in Console for enterprise to opt-in/adjust. (2 sprints)
4) Post-rollout tuning: adjust scoring weights and headroom heuristics, surface RBAC controls for enterprise admins. (ongoing)

Operational details:
- Config flags: routing.fhh.enabled (global), routing.fhh.regionOverrides (list), routing.fhh.tierDefaults, routing.fhh.max_headroom_pct
- DB persistence: headroom per region/tier cached in Redis with 30s TTL; store historical forecasts in time-series DB for audit.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator reproduces historical spend and eviction patterns and demonstrates reduced spend volatility in >= 3 of 5 regions
Routing can compute H(region,tier,customer) in <200ms and apply headroom without increasing P95 latency by >5% for hedged traffic
Console exposes headroom controls and per-customer spend forecast with a clear kill switch
Integration tests for spot eviction -> gradual on-demand ramping are added and passing in CI
Operational dashboards for unit cost, eviction rate, and headroom utilization are live before full rollout
